clue.text: City connected with Bath?

parts.note: reads as a cathedral city near the Somerset spa, but also as springs and water sources, the kind of thing one links with bathing

explanation.surface: A geography question about which city lies near Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells is a small cathedral city in Somerset, not far from Bath; wells also supply water, as baths need.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells is England's smallest cathedral city, close to the spa town of Bath, and wells are sources of bathwater.

clue.text: Couple New Year with a plea for divine guidance

parts.note: PR is the standard abbreviation for pair, a couple

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of year are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Two people mark the New Year by asking heaven for direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges YEAR into AYER, placed after PR.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is a petition addressed to God, often seeking help or direction.

clue.text: Push chair for one clearly able to walk at least slowly

definitions.meaning: a pushchair, a small folding seat on wheels for a baby

definitions.text: one clearly able to walk at least slowly
definitions.meaning: someone who saunters along at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A remark that a pushchair is for a child who can only just toddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroller is both an American name for a baby buggy and a person out for a leisurely walk.

clue.text: In the army our weapons are kept there

indicators.note: in tells us the word our sits inside the word army

explanation.surface: A claim about where the military stores its arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts OUR inside ARMY, between ARM and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoury is a store or arsenal where guns and other arms are held.

clue.text: Like the Light Brigade when only 300 came back utterly exhausted

definitions.text: Like the Light Brigade when only 300 came back
definitions.meaning: about six hundred rode in the Charge of the Light Brigade, so with only 300 returning, a fraction of one in two had perished
worn out, ready to drop

explanation.surface: A historical note on the Crimean War charge, then a description of extreme tiredness.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's poem has 'the six hundred' riding into the valley of death; half that number coming back means the other half were killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone completely worn out is said to be only partly alive, and the brigade lost about one in two of its riders.

clue.text: Intensively nurse patients with great pains

parts.note: to care for sick people is to nurse them
fully means thoroughly, to the utmost degree

explanation.surface: A hospital in which staff look after people suffering severe pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pains' looks like the patients' suffering, but 'with great pains' means taking trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking great pains over something means doing it with meticulous attention.

clue.text: Profit made by receiver who runs in to take the service

definitions.meaning: gain after costs are deducted

definitions.text: made by receiver who runs in to take the service
definitions.meaning: in tennis, a player receiving serve who rushes forward and hits the ball back from close to the mesh

explanation.surface: A tennis receiver charging forward to meet a serve, with a financial overtone.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings after deductions are a financial yield, and in tennis a shot back over the mesh from close in is a return played at the net.

clue.text: Woman unaffected by a reversal

indicators.note: the word reads identically from either end, so turning it round changes nothing

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A lady who takes a setback in her stride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversal' looks like a misfortune, but it means reading the word backwards, which leaves this palindrome unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a lady.

clue.text: Way up over fifty craft

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word way is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A route climbing over fifty boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns WAY into YAW, which sits over L.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing boat, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Attend the whist drive to perform without an orchestra

definitions.meaning: solo whist is a card game, so going to a whist drive could mean taking part in such a game
to give a performance unaccompanied

explanation.surface: Going to a card evening and giving an unaccompanied performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A whist drive is a social evening of card games, popular in British village halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a card game, and performing unaccompanied is a solo performance.

clue.text: A great king led far astray

indicators.note: gone astray, off the right path, so the letters wander into another order

explanation.surface: A mighty monarch leading his people far off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Astray' rearranges LEDFAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was a ninth-century king of Wessex who fought off the Vikings.

clue.text: Examination of the mouth

definitions.meaning: a spoken test, as for a language exam
relating to the mouth, as in hygiene

explanation.surface: A dental check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken test, and the adjective means relating to the mouth.

clue.text: Like the map of Europe after Pitt attended the party

definitions.text: Like the map of Europe after Pitt
definitions.meaning: after Napoleon's victory at Austerlitz, William Pitt said 'Roll up that map; it will not be wanted these ten years'
turned up at the celebration, arrived

explanation.surface: A history quip about Pitt the Younger, then someone arriving at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitt was the British Prime Minister; his remark about the map of Europe followed Austerlitz in 1805.
explanation.definitionFit: The map was wound into a tube, and someone who arrived at a party turned up, casually put.

clue.text: Evidence is lacking for instant coffee's clear advantage

definitions.meaning: there is no basis or justification for a claim
instant coffee leaves no sediment of ground beans in the cup

explanation.surface: A legal complaint mixed up with praise for instant coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any justification means having no basis, and soluble coffee leaves no dregs behind.

clue.text: Sporting awards that soldiers are called to

definitions.meaning: badges or caps given to members of a school or university team
soldiers are 'called to the flag', summoned to join the army

explanation.surface: Sports prizes and military summons combined.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools and universities, team members are awarded these as a mark of selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Team awards are given as badges or ribbons in house hues, and regimental flags are what recruits rally to.

clue.text: Maybe its musical attribution has yet to be settled

definitions.text: Maybe its musical attribution has yet to be settled

parts.words: Maybe its musical attribution has yet to be settled
parts.note: reads as an antique piece of written music of disputed authorship, but also as a longstanding grudge still awaiting revenge

explanation.surface: A musicologist's puzzle over who wrote a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a long-standing grievance waiting to be avenged; 'score' doubles as written music.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance held for years is an unsettled debt from long ago, and an aged piece of written music fits too.

clue.text: They wantonly destroy Kensington art museum and the Linnaean Society

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in South Kensington, London
LS stands for the Linnean Society of London, a natural history society

explanation.surface: A list of London cultural institutions that are under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is a London museum of art and design; the Linnean Society is a London scientific society.
explanation.definitionFit: Vandals are people who wilfully damage property, named after a Germanic tribe that sacked Rome.

clue.text: Wind's velocity over the whole of the country

definitions.text: over the whole of the country

parts.note: air is a gentle breeze, so a wind's could be air's
pace means speed

explanation.surface: A weather report on wind speed across the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind's velocity' looks like a single weather term, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the atmosphere above a nation's territory, which that state controls.

clue.text: British walk at an easy pace to find blackberries

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer names the plant that bears them, also used for its fruit

parts.note: to ramble is to stroll leisurely in the countryside

explanation.surface: A Briton out on a gentle country walk who goes looking for fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bramble is the prickly shrub whose dark fruit is picked in late summer.

clue.text: One who makes it in the world of drama?

definitions.text: One who makes it in the world of drama?

parts.words: One who makes it in the world of drama?
parts.note: reads as a successful actor, but also literally as the person who puts on a stage show

explanation.surface: A question about who succeeds in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes it' looks like 'succeeds', but here it means creating the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre producer finances and organises a stage show.

clue.text: Gadfly caught on the leg

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An insect landing on someone's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places C above LEG in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleg is a horsefly, a biting insect that pesters livestock.

clue.text: Carried away broken part

indicators.note: broken signals the word part is smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A component being taken away damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means enthralled, swept off one's feet with delight.

clue.text: Polite way to ask for a penny rent

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny in British money
a lease is a rental agreement

explanation.surface: A courteous request to borrow a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying please is the courteous formula used when making a request.

clue.text: Don is affected

definitions.meaning: to don clothes is to dress in them
pretended, assumed, as an affected manner

explanation.surface: A remark that a university lecturer is pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university lecturer or a name, but here it is the verb to dress in.
explanation.definitionFit: Donning a coat means dressing in it, and an affected manner is a feigned, assumed one.

clue.text: It gives strength to one's arm

definitions.text: It gives strength to one's arm

parts.words: It gives strength to one's arm
parts.note: reads like a motto about encouragement, but literally describes the tissue that powers a limb

explanation.surface: Something that encourages a person to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle is the contractile tissue that gives the body physical power.

clue.text: What the army did after flushing out the main enemy body?

definitions.text: What the army did after flushing out the main enemy body?

parts.words: What the army did after flushing out the main enemy body?
parts.note: reads as a military clearing-up of stragglers, while flushing suggests water spilt that needs wiping away

explanation.surface: A report on troops dealing with the remnants of an enemy force.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means dealing with remaining pockets of resistance; 'flushing' hints at cleaning with a mop.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops who clear out remaining resistance are said to finish off the job, as a cleaner wipes a floor.

clue.text: Deck for a party by the navy

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A ship's deck prepared for a naval celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a ship's floor, but here it is the verb to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a hall with holly is to decorate or embellish it.

clue.text: Once thought a beauty patch, now a dangerous bit of road

definitions.meaning: a small dark patch worn on the face as a fashion in the 17th and 18th centuries

definitions.text: now a dangerous bit of road
definitions.meaning: a stretch of road where accidents often happen

explanation.surface: How a dark mark went from fashionable to a road hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark beauty patch on the face was fashionable once, and an accident-prone road stretch carries the same name.
